body:
LM Windham @bluebon.net wrote -- among other things--

"Just what exactly defines 'the genius mind?'  Is it a certain level of
IQ?  Is it a certain level of antisocialization?  Is it a certain elevated
level of intellectual snobbery?"

I'd have to say that any true genius, far from being an intellectual snob,
would be likely to be humble about his gifts, as was Sir Isaac Newton --
because a superior intelligence is always aware of how much it will never
be able to grasp.  So that would probably exclude those who sneer at the
"average" person (who is probably far too busy doing backbreaking and/or
mind-numbing labor to be contemplating the future of society or the
meaning of life).

Is the Manifesto a "total ripoff of Ellul's ideas," Ms. Windham wonders? 
Well, Ellul's book "The Technological Society" was quoted and discussed in
this group several months ago, as part of Ross' "Find That Author" game. 
The ideas are, indeed, very similar to those expressed in the Manifesto,
although they are much more gracefully expressed, with an aristocratic
flair that Dave Buchanan compared to William F. Buckley.  (Needless to
say, there are no long digressions about leftism and political
correctness, as the book was written in the early '60s, I think.) The
Manifesto's author certainly puts his own spin on Ellul's ideas, IMHO, but
I don't say that as a compliment!

Ms. Windham very strikingly cites this passage:  "In para 125 we used an
analogy of a weak neighbor who is left destitute by a strong neighbor who
takes all his land by forcing on him a series of compromises... The only
sensible alternative for the weaker man is to kill the strong one while he
has the chance."  

Actually, that's the only homicidal alternative.  What about enlisting the
help of the other neighbors to battle the strong neighbor, refusing to
accept the compromises, and finding a creative solution to the problem? 
In other words, forming relationships with people, entering society and
using the law, rather than brute force, to achieve a desired end.  

"My personal prediction for 1997:  TK will languish in jail, and the point
counterpointing, citing, debating, flagellating, interpreting and positing
will continue."  No arguments here!
